images.caption: Codex Sinaiticus: Mark ends at 16:8, and the closing title follows.
Codex Alexandrinus: the text runs on past 16:8 into verses 9 to 20.
Codex Washingtonianus: Mark 16:12-17, the long ending, with a saying after 16:14 found in no other Greek manuscript (the “Freer Logion”).
images.author: Unknown author

images.caption: Codex Sinaiticus: the Lord’s Prayer ends “but deliver us from evil”, with no “for thine is the kingdom”.
images.author: Unknown author

images.caption: Codex Washingtonianus: the Lord’s Prayer with the closing words “for thine is the kingdom and the power and the glory for ever, amen”.
Codex Sinaiticus, 1 John 5:7-8: “there are three that testify, the Spirit and the water and the blood”, with nothing of the Father, the Word and the Holy Ghost.
Codex Sinaiticus: John 7:52 runs straight on to 8:12, with no story of the woman between.
